title: Motie van het lid Beckerman over een bevoegde instantie aanwijzen om ook deepfakeporno en andere onrechtmatige seksuele beelden offline te halen

reading.body:
Deepfake pornographic videos of Dutch public figures, including celebrities, politicians, and members of the Royal Family, appeared on an online platform without their consent or knowledge. The system created sexually explicit synthetic media by applying generative AI to real images of identifiable people. This is a failure of platform moderation and governance, where content that violates laws against revenge pornography was permitted to exist and spread to millions of users.

The deployment lacked adequate safeguards at multiple points. The platform allowed uploads of non-consensual intimate imagery, incentivized their creation through payments tied to views, and enabled uploaders to remain anonymous to avoid legal consequences. Detection and removal of deepfake pornography requires either human review of flagged content or technical systems trained to identify synthetic media, neither of which appears to have been in place or effective.

Whether the platform operators knowingly enabled this abuse, or whether technical detection systems for synthetic media existed but failed, is not established by the reporting. The incident prompted legal complaints, calls for government intervention, and proposals for a designated authority to remove such content from the internet.

summary:
Several female Dutch celebrities are considering legal action after appearing in manipulated pornographic videos on an online platform that receives 13 million monthly visitors. The platform contains fake videos featuring Dutch artists, television presenters, Olympic athletes, current and former government ministers, mayors, and members of the Royal Family. Justice Minister Yesilgöz called the videos disgusting and urged victims to file complaints. Managers and representatives of various victims confirmed they have filed reports or are considering legal action.

Deepfake pornography falls under revenge porn laws and is prosecutable. Users who upload material to the platform are advised to remain anonymous, likely to avoid prosecution, and are paid more if their videos receive many views. Lawyer Jelle Wieringa warned that more fake videos will emerge unless the government takes action. Victims can file reports, which may lead the Public Prosecutor to shut down the website, or pursue other options including mass claims, complaints to data protection authorities, or contacting hosting companies. Previously, presenter Welmoed Sijtsma was victimized by such videos and made a documentary about her experience, resulting in a 39-year-old man receiving a conditional sentence of 180 hours.
title_en: Motion by member Beckerman on designating a competent authority to also remove deepfake pornography and other unlawful sexual images offline
